relations.definition: A relationship indicating two individuals are romantically involved or engaged.
relations.embedding_query_text: partner_of: A relationship indicating two individuals are romantically involved or engaged.

candidates.label: spouse
candidates.comment: A marital relation between two persons who are married to each other. Also called "husband", "wife", "married to", "partner". Examples: "John has spouse Jane", "Mary's spouse is David", "The couple includes a spouse relationship.". Distinct from colleague, which indicates a professional relationship, or parent, which indicates a familial relationship.

candidates.label: knows
candidates.comment: A general acquaintance relation between two people who are known to each other socially or professionally. Also called acquainted with, familiar with, knows personally, has met. Examples: John knows 'Jane'. Sarah knows 'her colleague Tom'. The CEO knows 'the board members'. Distinct from follows, friend, or memberOf, which imply more specific types of relationships.

candidates.label: inverseOf
candidates.comment: A property relationship indicating that two properties describe the same association between entities but in opposite directions. Also called reciprocal property, opposite property, reverse property. Examples: The 'alumni' property is an inverseOf 'alumniOf'. The 'parent' property is an inverseOf 'child'. The 'employee' property is an inverseOf 'worksFor'.

candidates.label: sibling
candidates.comment: A familial relationship between two people who share at least one parent. Also called brother, sister, kin, family member. Examples: `John Doe` sibling `Jane Doe`, `Mary Smith` sibling `Tom Smith`, `Alice Brown` sibling `Bob Brown`. Distinct from `siblings`, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: relatedTo
candidates.comment: A familial relation between two people, representing a generic family connection. Also called family member, kin, relative. Examples: "John is related to 'Jane'.", "Mary is related to 'Tom'.", "Aunt Sally is related to 'Nephew Bob'."

candidates.label: children
candidates.comment: A familial relation between a person and their child. Also called "offspring", "son", "daughter". Examples: "John children Jane", "Mary children Peter". Distinct from parent, which indicates the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: member
candidates.comment: A member relation between an organization or program membership and an organization or person belonging to it. Also called: belongs to, is a part of, participant in. Examples: "Club Organization member John Doe", "Team ProgramMembership member Jane Smith", "Alliance Organization member Partner Company". Distinct from memberOf, which expresses the inverse relationship.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: colleague
candidates.comment: A professional relation between a person and another person who is their colleague. Also called "co-worker", "associate", "professional peer". Examples: "John colleague Jane", "Professor Smith colleague 'https://example.com/prof-jones'". Distinct from colleagues, which is a plural form, though semantically similar.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

relations.definition: Denotes an entity taking part in an event.
relations.embedding_query_text: has_participant: Denotes an entity taking part in an event.

candidates.label: hasParticipationOffer
candidates.comment: A participation offer relation between an event and an offer to participate in it. Also called call for participation, participation opportunity, event entry offer. Examples: "An event has a participation offer for speakers.", "The conference has a participation offer for proposals.", "This festival includes a participation offer for performers.". Distinct from hasSponsorshipOffer, which is an offer to sponsor the event.

candidates.label: participant
candidates.comment: A collaborative relation between an action and an organization or person who indirectly participated in it. Also called collaborated with, involved, assisted by, co-agent. Examples: A writing action has a participant co-author. A research project has a participant researcher. A meeting has a participant attendee. Distinct from agent, which is the primary actor of an action.

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: hasSponsorshipOffer
candidates.comment: A sponsorship offer relation between an event and an offer to sponsor it. Also called sponsorship opportunity, sponsor package, call for sponsors. Examples: "An event has a sponsorship offer for corporate partners.", "The conference has a sponsorship offer with different tiers.", "This festival includes a sponsorship offer.". Distinct from hasParticipationOffer, which is an offer to participate in the event.

candidates.label: performers
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and its primary performers, who can be organizations or persons. Also called main artists, headliners, principal actors, featured performers. Examples: A concert has performers 'Coldplay'. A play has performers 'The Royal Shakespeare Company'. A festival has performers 'Various Artists'. Distinct from performer, which can be any performer, not necessarily the main one.

relations.definition: The location where an event takes place.
relations.embedding_query_text: occurs_at: The location where an event takes place.

instances: Wedding celebration kickoff -> Madison Square Garden

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: sportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A specific location relation between an exercise action and the sports activity venue where it took place. Also called "exercise location", "training venue", "athletic facility", "gym location". Examples: "The run had sportsActivityLocation Central Park", "The workout's sportsActivityLocation was the local gym", "This exercise action took place at a sportsActivityLocation stadium.". Distinct from location, which is a more general location property.

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: entertainmentBusiness
candidates.comment: An entertainment business relation between a perform action and the entertainment business where the action occurred. Also called "venue", "performance location", "showplace". Examples: "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Concert Hall'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Theater Royal'", "Perform action entertainmentBusiness 'Comedy Club'". Distinct from location, which is a more general property for any place an action occurs.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: foodEvent
candidates.comment: A food event relation between a cook action and the specific food-related event where the cooking took place. Also called: culinary event, cooking event, gastronomic occasion. Examples: "Chef prepares meal" food event "Annual Food Festival", "Home Cook makes dinner" food event "Family Dinner Party", "Baker bakes bread" food event "Charity Bake Sale". Distinct from foodEstablishment, which is a specific place.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

relations.definition: Indicates that a place is situated within a larger geographic area.
relations.embedding_query_text: located_in: Indicates that a place is situated within a larger geographic area.

instances: Madison Square Garden -> New York City

candidates.label: containedIn
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedIn 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedIn 'Paris'". Distinct from containedInPlace, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: containedInPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and the larger place that contains it. Also called "located in", "part of", "within". Examples: "City 'Paris' containedInPlace 'France'", "Building 'Eiffel Tower' containedInPlace 'Paris'". Distinct from containedIn, which is a synonym, and containsPlace, which is the inverse.

candidates.label: geoWithin
candidates.comment: A geo within relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is located entirely inside the interior of another containing geometry or place. Also called: is inside, contained in, located within. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo within "Country 'France'", "Office 'Suite 100'" geo within "Building 'Empire State'", "State 'California'" geo within "Country 'USA'". Distinct from geoContains, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: geo
candidates.comment: A geo relation between a place and its geographical coordinates or shape. Also called: geographic location, coordinates, spatial data. Examples: "Eiffel Tower" geo "Latitude: 48.8584, Longitude: 2.2945", "Central Park" geo "Polygon GeoShape", "Mount Everest" geo "Point GeoCoordinates".

candidates.label: longitude
candidates.comment: A longitude relation between geographic coordinates or a place and its longitudinal value. Also called: geographic longitude, east-west coordinate, meridian position. Examples: "Eiffel Tower longitude 2.2945", "Statue of Liberty longitude -74.0445", "Mount Everest longitude 86.9250".

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: geographicArea
candidates.comment: A geographic area relation between an audience and the administrative area it is associated with. Also called: target region, audience location, demographic area. Examples: "Local News Audience" geographic area "Springfield County", "National Election Voters" geographic area "United States", "European Market Audience" geographic area "European Union".

candidates.label: latitude
candidates.comment: A geographical coordinate relation between geo-coordinates or a place and its north-south position on the Earth's surface. Also called lat, north-south coordinate, parallel. Examples: GeoCoordinates have a latitude of '34.0522'. A place has a latitude of '-33.8688'. The city's latitude is '40.7128'. Distinct from longitude, which is the east-west position.

candidates.label: containsPlace
candidates.comment: A spatial containment relation between a place and another smaller place that it contains. Also called "includes place", "encompasses", "holds". Examples: "Country 'France' containsPlace 'Paris'", "City 'Paris' containsPlace 'Eiffel Tower'". Distinct from containedIn or containedInPlace, which are the inverse relations.

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

relations.definition: Associates an event with a specific calendar date or time.
relations.embedding_query_text: has_date: Associates an event with a specific calendar date or time.

chosen_property.label: hasDate
chosen_property.definition: Associates an event or permit with a specific calendar date or time range.
chosen_property.justification: No existing schema.org property matches Event/Permit → DateRange without losing meaning.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: exceptDate
candidates.comment: An exception date relation between a schedule and a specific date or datetime when a scheduled event will not take place. Also called: exclusion date, cancelled date, unavailable date. Examples: "Weekly Yoga Class Schedule" except date "2023-12-25", "Daily Bus Route Schedule" except date "2024-01-01T08:00:00", "Monthly Book Club Schedule" except date "2023-11-11".

candidates.label: scheduledTime
candidates.comment: The specific date or date and time when an action is planned to occur. Also called planned time, scheduled date, appointment time. Examples: `Meeting Action` scheduledTime `2023-10-26T10:00:00`, `Delivery Action` scheduledTime `2023-11-01`, `Maintenance Action` scheduledTime `2023-12-05T14:30:00`.

candidates.label: contentReferenceTime
candidates.comment: A temporal reference relation for a creative work, indicating the specific date and time described or emphasized within its content. Also called "event time", "depicted time", "time of content". Examples: "News article contentReferenceTime '2023-10-26T14:00:00Z'", "Historical documentary contentReferenceTime '1945-09-02'".

candidates.label: endDate
candidates.comment: An end date relation between an item (such as a season, event, or schedule) and the date and time when it concludes. Also called "conclusion date", "finish date", "termination date". Examples: "Event 'Conference' endDate '2023-10-27'", "Creative work season endDate '2024-05-31'", "Role 'Project Manager' endDate '2025-12-31'". Distinct from endTime, which specifies the end time within a single day or for a clip.

candidates.label: startDate
candidates.comment: A temporal marker indicating the beginning date and time of an item, such as an event, program, or season. Also called "beginning date", "commencement date", "start time", "effective date". Examples: "The event has startDate 2023-10-26", "The program's startDate is September 1st", "This role's startDate was last Monday.". Distinct from dateCreated, which indicates when a creative work was first made.

candidates.label: temporal
candidates.comment: A general temporal relation between a creative work and a date or time, used when more specific temporal properties are not applicable. Also called "related to time", "time context", "associated temporal period", "timeframe". Examples: "The novel has temporal the 19th century", "The painting's temporal is the Renaissance era", "This document's temporal is the year 2020.". Distinct from temporalCoverage, which indicates the specific time period the content applies to.

candidates.label: previousStartDate
candidates.comment: A temporal attribute indicating the previously scheduled start date for an event that has been rescheduled or cancelled. Also called original start date, former start date, initial event date. Examples: A rescheduled event has a previous start date of '2023-03-15'. The cancelled concert had a previous start date of '2023-07-01T19:00:00'. The postponed meeting's previous start date was 'last Monday'. Distinct from startDate, which is the current or newly scheduled start date.

candidates.label: deathDate
candidates.comment: A temporal event relation between a person and their date of death. Also called: date of demise, passing date, decease date. Examples: "Historical Figure" death date "1963-11-22", "Family Member" death date "2020-05-10". Distinct from birthDate, which is the date of birth.

candidates.label: doorTime
candidates.comment: A door time relation between an event and the date or time when admission will commence. Also called "admission time", "entry time", "gate opening time". Examples: "Concert event doorTime '19:00'", "Theater show doorTime '2023-11-01T18:30'", "Festival doorTime '10:00'".

relations.definition: Indicates a donor gave resources to a recipient organization.
relations.embedding_query_text: donated_to: Indicates a donor gave resources to a recipient organization.

candidates.label: recipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation between an action (like sending or paying) and the audience, contact point, organization, or person receiving it. Also called receiver, intended for, sent to. Examples: "A message has a recipient 'John Doe'.", "A donation has a recipient 'Charity Organization'.", "A payment has a recipient 'Vendor Inc.'."

candidates.label: fundedItem
candidates.comment: A funded item relation between a grant and the biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product that receives direct or indirect funding or sponsorship. Also called: grant recipient, sponsored item, supported entity. Examples: "Research Grant" funded item "Cancer Research Project", "Arts Grant" funded item "Local Theater Production", "Educational Grant" funded item "Student Scholarship Program". Distinct from funding, which is the grant itself.

candidates.label: ccRecipient
candidates.comment: A recipient relation for a message, indicating a contact point, organization, or person who is copied on it. Also called "carbon copy recipient", "copied to", "CC'd party". Examples: "Email message ccRecipient John Doe", "Internal memo message ccRecipient HR Department".

candidates.label: funding
candidates.comment: A funding relation between a biochemical entity, creative work, event, medical entity, organization, person, or product and the grant that provides its direct or indirect financial support. Also called: grant received, sponsorship, financial support. Examples: "Cancer Research Project" funding "NIH Grant R01", "Local Theater Production" funding "Arts Council Grant", "Student Scholarship Program" funding "University Endowment Grant". Distinct from funder, which is the entity providing the funding.

candidates.label: endorsee
candidates.comment: An endorsee relation between an endorse action and the person or organization being supported. Also called "supported entity", "beneficiary", "recipient of endorsement". Examples: "Endorse action endorsee 'Candidate A'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Charity B'", "Endorse action endorsee 'Product C'". Distinct from endorsers, which are the people or organizations providing the endorsement.

candidates.label: funder
candidates.comment: A funder relation between a creative work, event, grant, organization, or person and the organization or person providing financial support or sponsorship. Also called: sponsor, benefactor, financial supporter. Examples: "Art Exhibition" funder "National Endowment for the Arts", "Research Project" funder "NIH", "Charity Event" funder "Local Bank". Distinct from fundedItem, which is the item receiving funding.

candidates.label: toRecipient
candidates.comment: A direct recipient relation between a message and the specific audience, contact point, organization, or person it was sent to. Also called direct addressee, message recipient, primary recipient. Examples: "Email toRecipient 'john.doe@example.com'", "Message toRecipient 'Marketing Department'", "SMS toRecipient 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from recipient, which is a more general property for any recipient.

candidates.label: contributor
candidates.comment: A secondary participation relation for a creative work or event, indicating an organization or person who contributed to it. Also called "additional contributor", "supporting role", "collaborator". Examples: "Book creative work contributor 'Editor Jane Doe'", "Conference event contributor 'Sponsor Acme Corp'". Distinct from author or creator, which typically denote primary responsibility.

candidates.label: isGift
candidates.comment: A transaction intent relation indicating whether an order was placed as a gift for a recipient other than the buyer. Also called gift purchase, purchased as gift, gift order. Examples: An order has isGift set to 'true'. A purchase has isGift set to 'false'. A book order has isGift set to 'true' with gift wrapping.

candidates.label: beneficiaryBank
candidates.comment: A bank, branch, or financial institution operating the beneficiary's bank account or releasing funds for a money transfer. Also called: recipient bank, receiving bank, destination bank. Examples: "MoneyTransfer 'Wire Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'Bank of America'", "MoneyTransfer 'International Transfer' beneficiaryBank 'HSBC'."

relations.definition: Links a claim or statement to the event or subject it discusses.
relations.embedding_query_text: refers_to: Links a claim or statement to the event or subject it discusses.

instances: Representatives say donation for charities -> Charity donation
No phones allowed at ceremony -> Wedding celebration kickoff
Mayor alludes to wedding chatter -> Wedding celebration kickoff

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". Distinct from associatedMediaReview, which links to a media review.

candidates.label: associatedMediaReview
candidates.comment: A media review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related media review, linked media assessment. Examples: "Review 'ClaimReview of Statement' associatedMediaReview 'MediaReview of Article'", "Review 'ProductReview' associatedMediaReview 'VideoReview'". Distinct from associatedClaimReview, which links to a claim review.

candidates.label: about
candidates.comment: A subject matter relation between an entity (e.g., a creative work, event, or communication) and the topic it concerns. Also called concerning, regarding, on the topic of, related to. Examples: "A book about quantum physics.", "A lecture about climate change.", "A certification about data privacy."

candidates.label: associatedArticle
candidates.comment: A news article linked to a media object. Also called: related article, accompanying article, news story link. Examples: "MediaObject 'Video of Protest' associatedArticle 'NewsArticle on Protest'", "MediaObject 'Photo of Event' associatedArticle 'Article about Event'."

candidates.label: subjectOf
candidates.comment: A thematic relation between a thing and a creative work or event that is about it. Also called "topic of", "depicted in", "featured in", "covered by". Examples: "The person is subjectOf a biography", "The historical event is subjectOf a documentary", "This concept is subjectOf a research paper."

candidates.label: mentions
candidates.comment: A mention relation between a creative work and a thing it references without necessarily being about. Also called: references, alludes to, cites. Examples: "News Article mentions 'Climate Change'", "Book mentions 'Historical Event'", "Speech mentions 'Famous Person'". Distinct from about, which indicates the primary topic of the creative work.

candidates.label: discusses
candidates.comment: A discussion relation between a user comment and the creative work it is associated with. Also called "comments on", "pertains to", "about". Examples: "User comment 'Great movie!' discusses 'The Matrix'", "Blog post comment discusses 'Article on AI'", "Review discusses 'New Album by Artist X'". Distinct from discussionUrl, which is a link to the page containing comments about a creative work.

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.label: interpretedAsClaim
candidates.comment: A claim extraction relation between a creative work or media object and a specific assertion or statement derived from its content. Also called contains claim, implies claim, claim extracted from, claim derived from. Examples: A news article is interpretedAsClaim 'The sky is blue'. A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: claimInterpreter
candidates.comment: An interpretation relation between a claim and the organization or person who interpreted it from media content. Also called "interpreted by", "claim analyst", "fact-checker". Examples: "News claim claimInterpreter FactCheck.org", "Social media claim claimInterpreter Jane Doe".

relations.definition: Specifies the authority that produced or authorized a document or permit.
relations.embedding_query_text: issued_by: Specifies the authority that produced or authorized a document or permit.

candidates.label: issuedBy
candidates.comment: An issuing authority relation between a certification, permit, or ticket and the organization that granted or provided it. Also called granted by, provided by, authorized by, issuer. Examples: A driver's license is issuedBy 'Department of Motor Vehicles'. A concert ticket is issuedBy 'Ticketmaster'. A professional certification is issuedBy 'Certification Body X'.

candidates.label: issuedThrough
candidates.comment: A service channel relation between a permit and the specific service used to obtain it. Also called obtained via, granted through, service channel. Examples: A building permit was issuedThrough 'Online Permit Application System'. A fishing license was issuedThrough 'State Wildlife Service'. A visa was issuedThrough 'Consular Services Department'. Distinct from issuedBy, which is the organization, not the service.

candidates.label: validFor
candidates.comment: A valid for relation between a credential or permit and the duration of its validity. Also called duration of validity, valid period, effective duration. Examples: "Permit validFor 'P1Y'", "Credential validFor 'P5Y'", "License validFor 'P6M'".

candidates.label: grantee
candidates.comment: A grantee relation between a digital document permission and the audience, contact point, organization, or person to whom the permission is granted. Also called: permission recipient, authorized party, beneficiary. Examples: "Document Access Permission" grantee "Team Members", "File Sharing Permission" grantee "John Doe", "API Access Permission" grantee "Developer Organization".

candidates.label: legislationPassedBy
candidates.comment: A passing authority relation between a piece of legislation and the organization or person that originally enacted it. Also called: enacted by, made by, legislated by. Examples: "Primary Legislation legislationPassedBy Parliament", "Secondary Legislation legislationPassedBy Government", "Local Bylaw legislationPassedBy City Council". Distinct from legislationResponsible, which refers to the ministry or individual in charge of elaborating or addressing questions about the legislation.

candidates.label: dateIssued
candidates.comment: A temporal issuance relation between a ticket and the date it was issued. Also called: issuance date, date of issue, ticket date. Examples: "Concert Ticket" date issued "2023-04-01", "Flight Ticket" date issued "2023-01-10T14:30:00Z", "Parking Permit" date issued "2023-07-01".

candidates.label: publisher
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a creative work or financial incentive and the organization or person that publishes it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book has a publisher 'Penguin Random House'.", "A research paper has a publisher 'Nature Publishing Group'.", "A financial incentive has a publisher 'Government Agency'.". Distinct from publishedBy, which refers to the agent of a specific publication event.

candidates.label: publishedBy
candidates.comment: A publisher relation between a publication event and the organization or person responsible for it. Also called published by, issued by, released by. Examples: "A book's publication event was published by 'Penguin Random House'.", "A journal article's publication event was published by 'Elsevier'.", "A blog post's publication event was published by 'Jane Doe'.". Distinct from publisher, which refers to the publisher of the creative work itself.

candidates.label: validUntil
candidates.comment: A valid until relation between a permit and the date it ceases to be valid. Also called permit expiration date, permit end date, validity end date. Examples: "Permit validUntil '2024-06-30'", "Permit validUntil '2025-01-01'", "Permit validUntil '2023-12-31'". Distinct from validThrough, which is a more general property for various items.

candidates.label: validIn
candidates.comment: A valid in relation between a certification, credential, or permit and the geographic area where it is valid. Also called valid region, applicable area, geographic validity. Examples: "Permit validIn 'California'", "Certification validIn 'European Union'", "Credential validIn 'United States'".

relations.definition: Indicates a person was present at an event.

candidates.label: attendee

candidates.label: attendees
candidates.comment: A person present at an event. Also called: participants, guests, visitors. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendees 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendees 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendees 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendee, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: A physical attendee capacity relation between an event and the maximum number of individuals who can physically attend. Also called: in-person capacity, venue limit, on-site capacity. Examples: "Hybrid Conference maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 500", "Live Concert maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 10000", "Workshop maximumPhysicalAttendeeCapacity 30". Distinct from maximumVirtualAttendeeCapacity, which refers to online attendees.

candidates.label: eventAttendanceMode
candidates.comment: An event attendance mode relation between an event and the enumeration indicating whether it occurs online, offline, or a mix. Also called "attendance format", "event delivery mode", "participation mode". Examples: "Event 'Conference' eventAttendanceMode 'OnlineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Workshop' eventAttendanceMode 'OfflineEventAttendanceMode'", "Event 'Hybrid Meeting' eventAttendanceMode 'MixedEventAttendanceMode'".

candidates.label: maximumAttendeeCapacity
candidates.comment: An attendee capacity relation between an event or place and the total number of individuals it can accommodate. Also called: maximum occupancy, total capacity, attendee limit. Examples: "Concert Venue maximumAttendeeCapacity 5000", "Conference Room maximumAttendeeCapacity 100", "Public Park maximumAttendeeCapacity 10000".

candidates.label: remainingAttendeeCapacity

Examples: "A concert has a remaining attendee capacity of 100.", "A workshop has a remaining attendee capacity of 5.", "A conference has a remaining attendee capacity of 500."

candidates.label: performer
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between an event and an organization or person who performs at it. Also called artist, entertainer, presenter, actor. Examples: A concert has a performer 'Taylor Swift'. A play has a performer 'Meryl Streep'. A conference has a performer 'Dr. Jane Doe'. Distinct from performerIn, which points from a person to an event.

candidates.label: performerIn
candidates.comment: A participation role relation between a person and an event in which they perform or participate. Also called performs in, participates in, acts in, presents at. Examples: John Doe is a performer in 'The Annual Gala'. Jane Smith is a performer in 'The City Marathon'. An actor is a performer in 'The New Play'. Distinct from performer, which points from an event to a person.

candidates.label: competitor
candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

A scientific paper is interpretedAsClaim 'Drug X cures Y'. A video is interpretedAsClaim 'Candidate Z made promise A'.

candidates.label: commentTime

candidates.label: resultComment

Examples: `CommentAction on Article` resultComment `User's Comment Text`, `ReplyAction to Forum Post` resultComment `Reply Comment`, `ReviewAction` resultComment `Reviewer's Feedback`. Distinct from `result`, which is a general outcome of any action.

candidates.label: commentCount
candidates.comment: A quantitative measurement for a creative work, indicating the total number of comments it has received. Also called "number of comments", "comment total", "feedback count". Examples: "Blog post commentCount 15", "Article commentCount 200".

candidates.label: appearance
candidates.comment: An appearance relation between a claim and a creative work where that claim is found or occurs. Also called occurrence in, mentioned in, found in. Examples: "A claim's appearance is in 'News Article X'.", "The factual claim's appearance is in 'Research Paper Y'."

candidates.label: associatedClaimReview
candidates.comment: A claim review related to another review by common content, topic, or claim. Also called: related claim review, linked claim assessment. Examples: "Review 'MediaReview of Article' associatedClaimReview 'ClaimReview of Statement'", "Review 'FactCheck' associatedClaimReview 'Another FactCheck'". candidates.label: creator
candidates.comment: An authorship relation between a creative work or user comment and the person or organization responsible for its creation. Also called: author, originator, producer, made by. Examples: "Novel" creator "Jane Doe", "Software" creator "Acme Corp.", "Blog Post" creator "John Smith", "User Review" creator "Anonymous User". Distinct from copyrightHolder, which is about legal ownership.

candidates.label: firstAppearance
candidates.comment: A first appearance relation between a claim and the creative work where it was initially known to occur. Also called: initial publication, original mention, debut in. Examples: "Claim: Earth is flat" first appearance "Ancient Greek Texts", "Claim: COVID-19 is a hoax" first appearance "Social Media Post", "Claim: New drug cures cancer" first appearance "Unverified Online Article".

candidates.label: claimReviewed
candidates.comment: A summary relation for a claim review, providing a short text of the specific claims being reviewed. Also called "reviewed claim", "claim summary", "subject of review". Examples: "Fact-check review claimReviewed 'Eating apples cures cancer'", "Product claim review claimReviewed 'This product doubles battery life'".

candidates.comment: A participation relation in a sports event, indicating a person or sports team that is competing. Also called "participant", "opponent", "rival". Examples: "Olympic race sports event competitor Usain Bolt", "Football match sports event competitor Manchester United".

Examples: "A medical risk estimator includes a risk factor of age.", "The estimator considers an included risk factor of smoking.", "This tool uses an included risk factor for calculation."

chosen_property.label: expectedGuestsNumber
chosen_property.definition: Specifies the expected number of guests for an event permit.
chosen_property.justification: No existing property captures EventPermit → Number for guest count.

candidates.label: additionalNumberOfGuests
candidates.comment: An additional number of guests relation between an RSVP action and the count of extra attendees beyond the invitee. Also called plus-one count, extra guests, total additional attendees. Examples: "An RSVP action's additional number of guests is '2'.", "The wedding RSVP indicates an additional number of guests of '1'."

candidates.label: expectedArrivalFrom
candidates.comment: An expected arrival from relation between a parcel delivery and the earliest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: earliest arrival, minimum delivery date, estimated start arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival from "2023-10-26", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival from "2023-10-27T09:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival from "2023-11-01". Distinct from expectedArrivalUntil, which is the latest arrival date.

candidates.label: expectedArrivalUntil
candidates.comment: An expected arrival until relation between a parcel delivery and the latest date or datetime the package is anticipated to arrive. Also called: latest arrival, maximum delivery date, estimated end arrival. Examples: "Amazon Order #123" expected arrival until "2023-10-28", "UPS Package #456" expected arrival until "2023-10-27T17:00:00", "International Shipment" expected arrival until "2023-11-05". Distinct from expectedArrivalFrom, which is the earliest arrival date.

candidates.label: partySize
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the number of people a reservation is intended to accommodate. Also called number of guests, group size, capacity for. Examples: A restaurant reservation has a party size of four. A taxi reservation has a party size of two. A hotel booking has a party size of three.

candidates.label: numAdults
candidates.comment: The number of adults included in a lodging reservation. Also called adult count, number of grown-ups, adult guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numAdults 2", "Vacation Rental numAdults 4", "Single Room Reservation numAdults 1". Distinct from numChildren, which specifies the number of children.

candidates.label: numChildren
candidates.comment: The number of children included in a lodging reservation. Also called child count, number of kids, child guests. Examples: "Hotel Reservation numChildren 1", "Vacation Rental numChildren 3", "Family Suite Reservation numChildren 2". Distinct from numAdults, which specifies the number of adults.

candidates.label: arrivalTime
candidates.comment: An expected time of arrival for a trip. Also called: estimated arrival, scheduled arrival, landing time. Examples: "Trip to NYC arrivalTime '2023-10-27T14:30:00'", "Flight 789 arrivalTime '18:00'", "Bus Trip arrivalTime 'tomorrow 09:15'."

candidates.label: passengerSequenceNumber
candidates.comment: A descriptive attribute indicating the sequence number assigned to a passenger for a flight reservation by the airline. Also called boarding sequence, passenger number, flight sequence. Examples: A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '001'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number 'A12'. A flight reservation has a passenger sequence number '34B'.

candidates.label: occupancy
candidates.comment: The allowed total occupancy in persons for an accommodation unit. Also called maximum occupancy, guest capacity, permitted persons. Examples: "Hotel Room occupancy 2", "Apartment occupancy 4", "Suite occupancy 6".

candidates.label: attendee
candidates.comment: A person or organization present at an event. Also called: participant, guest, visitor. Examples: "Event 'Concert' attendee 'John Doe'", "Event 'Conference' attendee 'Acme Corp'", "Event 'Meeting' attendee 'Jane Smith'". Distinct from attendees, which is the plural form.
